# RC-001 QLD8 Higgs-source square: derivative and Fierz-channel census

**Date:** 2026-11-10  
**Workstream:** PR #11, fermionic source-operator reduction  
**Scope:** enumerate the independent source-pair channels generated by \((D_\mu\mathcal J_H)^\dagger D^\mu\mathcal J_H\), classify their chiral/color/weak structures, and identify what the fermion EOM can and cannot remove. This is a pre-Fierz census, not a completed nonredundant basis.

## 1. Source decomposition

Use the original flavor-diagonal axial-model source from [RC-001-QLD-Higgs-source-EOM-model-map.md](RC-001-QLD-Higgs-source-EOM-model-map.md):
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal J_H^k&=\mathcal J_d^k+\mathcal J_u^k+\mathcal J_e^k+\mathcal J_H^{(5),k}+\cdots,\\
\mathcal J_d^k&=\bar d_{R\,a}Y_d^\dagger Q_{L\,a}^k,\\
\mathcal J_u^k&=\epsilon_{ik}\bar Q_{L\,a}^{\,i}Y_u u_{R\,a},\\
\mathcal J_e^k&=y_e^*\bar e_R L_e^k.
\end{aligned}
\]
Here \(a\) is a color index, weak indices are \(i,k\), and quark generation indices are contracted with the full Yukawa matrices. The \(C_5\) axial source is higher order for the strict \(O(M_E^{-4})\) operators and is omitted from this leading source-square census.

The source-square term is
\[
\mathcal O_{S,\mathrm{src}}^{(8)}
=\sum_k(D_\mu\mathcal J_H^k)^\dagger D^\mu\mathcal J_H^k
=\sum_{A,B=d,u,e}\sum_k
(D_\mu\mathcal J_A^k)^\dagger D^\mu\mathcal J_B^k
+O(M_E^{-5}).
\]
There are nine ordered source pairs. Equivalently, they form three diagonal structures and three cross structures plus their Hermitian conjugates:
\[
d^\dagger d,\quad u^\dagger u,\quad e^\dagger e,\quad
(d^\dagger u+\mathrm{h.c.}),\quad
(d^\dagger e+\mathrm{h.c.}),\quad
(u^\dagger e+\mathrm{h.c.}).
\]
Each derivative of a bilinear obeys a two-term product rule. Thus each ordered pair produces four derivative placements if fully expanded. Those placements are algebraic terms within one source-pair structure, not independent Wilson coefficients.

## 2. Chiral and representation classification

The scalar bilinear projectors are:
\[
\mathcal J_d\sim\bar d_R Q_L,\qquad
\mathcal J_u\sim\bar Q_L u_R,\qquad
\mathcal J_e\sim\bar e_R L_e.
\]
The source-pair classification is:

| Source pair | Representative scalar product before derivatives | Chiral class | Additional index structure |
|---|---|---|---|
| \(d^\dagger d\) | \((\bar Q_L d_R)(\bar d_R Q_L)\) | opposite-projector scalar pair; Fierz to vector-current type | two quark color contractions; retain singlet/octet or equivalent crossed-color basis |
| \(u^\dagger u\) | \((\bar u_R Q_L)(\bar Q_L u_R)\) | opposite-projector scalar pair; Fierz to vector-current type | two quark color contractions; retain singlet/octet or equivalent crossed-color basis |
| \(e^\dagger e\) | \((\bar L_e e_R)(\bar e_R L_e)\) | opposite-projector scalar pair; Fierz to vector-current type | color singlet |
| \(d^\dagger e\) | \((\bar Q_L d_R)(\bar e_R L_e)\) | opposite-projector scalar pair; Fierz to vector-current type | quark-lepton current structure; color carried by the quark bilinear |
| \(d^\dagger u\) | \(\epsilon_{ik}(\bar Q_L^k d_R)(\bar Q_L^i u_R)\) | same-projector scalar pair; scalar/tensor Fierz structures must be retained | antisymmetric weak contraction; nontrivial quark color/flavor contractions |
| \(u^\dagger e\) | \(\epsilon_{ik}(\bar u_R Q_L^i)(\bar e_R L_e^k)\) | same-projector scalar pair; scalar/tensor Fierz structures must be retained | antisymmetric weak contraction; quark-lepton structure |

The reverse cross pairs are the Hermitian conjugates. No cross pair is discarded merely because its two source bilinears are different: all three source components transform as the same Higgs doublet, so their pairwise products are gauge singlets. Any further zero must follow from an explicit weak, color, flavor, or Grassmann identity, not from an assumed absence of a source.

For the quark crossed-color contractions, the exact \(SU(3)_c\) completeness relation is
\[
T^A_{ab}T^A_{cd}
=\frac12\left(\delta_{ad}\delta_{cb}
-\frac1{N_c}\delta_{ab}\delta_{cd}\right),
\qquad N_c=3.
\]
It allows a crossed contraction to be represented in a singlet/octet basis after the spinor Fierz step. Do not replace a crossed contraction by a product of color-singlet currents without this decomposition.

## 3. Derivative placements

For any scalar source bilinear \(J=\bar f\,\chi\),
\[
D_\mu J=(D_\mu\bar f)\chi+\bar f(D_\mu\chi).
\]
Consequently
\[
(D_\mu J_A)^\dagger D^\mu J_B
\]
contains four product-rule placements: derivative on the first fermion in \(J_A^\dagger\) or on its partner, crossed with derivative on the first or second fermion in \(J_B\). The covariant derivatives carry the representations of the individual fields. They must not be replaced by ordinary derivatives before the gauge-current and EOM bookkeeping is completed.

Fierz identities act on the spinor contractions of each placement, but do not eliminate its derivative distribution. A basis reduction must keep the Lorentz derivative placement, weak contraction, color contraction, and flavor tensors as separate labels until IBP and EOM relations are applied.

## 4. Fermion EOM limitation

The leading Dirac equations determine \(\slashed D\psi\), not a free-index \(D_\mu\psi\). In \(d\) dimensions,
\[
D_\mu\psi=\frac1d\gamma_\mu\slashed D\psi+D_\mu^\perp\psi,
\qquad
\gamma^\mu D_\mu^\perp\psi=0.
\]
The EOM can replace the gamma-trace part. The gamma-traceless vector-spinor component remains. Therefore the source-square operators cannot be removed by a blanket fermion-EOM substitution. The same limitation applies to the two-fermion \(F_A^{\mu\nu}D_\mu\mathcal J_H D_\nu H\) source operator.

For a dimensionally regulated matching, the Fierz identities must be fixed in \(d=4-2\epsilon\). Four-dimensional Fierz rearrangements alone can miss evanescent operators whose \(O(\epsilon)\) coefficients multiply UV poles.

## 5. What is closed and what remains open

Closed in this census:
- the three leading-renormalizable Higgs-source components for the original flavor-diagonal model;
- the nine ordered source-pair channels, or three diagonal plus three cross pairs and their conjugates;
- the chiral class and the required color/weak/flavor labels for each pair;
- the four product-rule derivative placements per ordered pair;
- the limitation of the fermion EOM to gamma-contracted derivatives.

Still open:
- explicit \(d\)-dimensional spinor Fierz reduction for each derivative placement;
- reduction of crossed color structures into a chosen singlet/octet basis;
- weak-index identities and flavor-tensor symmetries for the same-projector \(d^\dagger u\) and \(u^\dagger e\) channels;
- IBP reduction of derivative placements and the evanescent-operator counterterm basis;
- matching these operators against the complete same-order EFT soft graphs and counterterms.

No source-square coefficient is added to the PR #69 scalar two-point functions by this channel census.


## 6. Exact four-dimensional chiral Fierz projection

The spinor-only four-dimensional Fierz identities are now checked component by component in [RC-001-QLD-chiral-Fierz-identities.md](RC-001-QLD-chiral-Fierz-identities.md), using the exact SymPy matrix audit. The opposite-projector source pairs project to vector-current structures; the same-projector \(d^\dagger u\) and \(u^\dagger e\) pairs project to scalar-plus-tensor structures. The color and weak-index labels in this census remain attached to each rearranged bilinear.

The four-dimensional algebra is closed. The \(d\)-dimensional evanescent basis, its \(O(\epsilon)\) convention, and any loop-induced evanescent mixing are still open; the current audit does not claim a finite \(\overline{\mathrm{MS}}\) Wilson-vector reduction.


## 7. Derivative-aware Fierz and covariant-IBP ledger

The complete source-square derivative bookkeeping is now recorded in [RC-001-QLD8-derivative-Fierz-IBP-ledger.md](RC-001-QLD8-derivative-Fierz-IBP-ledger.md). It gives the exact action-level identity
\[
(D_\mu J_A^\dagger)(D^\mu J_B)\doteq-J_A^\dagger D^2J_B,
\]
the three Leibniz classes in \(D^2(\bar fY\chi)\), and the derivative-label map through the crossed spinor Fierz rearrangement. The four original placements are not individually identified by IBP; the identity applies to their complete sum.

The exact bookkeeping audit confirms nine ordered source pairs, four placements per ordered pair (36 total), and the \(RL/LR/RR/LL\) channel assignment. It is not a d-dimensional loop-mixing calculation and does not close the nonredundant dimension-eight basis.
